statement: A function $f$ defined on all real numbers satisfies $f(x) + x\,f(1 - x) = x^2$ for every real $x$. What is $f(3)$?

choices.misconception: I substituted $x = -2$ but wrote the coefficient as $3$ instead of $-2$, giving $f(-2) + 3f(3) = 4$.
I wrote the second equation as $f(-2) + 2f(3) = 4$, dropping the minus sign of $x = -2$.
I assumed $f(1 - x) = f(x)$, so with $x = 3$ I got $f(3) + 3f(3) = 9$.
I solved the system correctly but reported $f(-2)$ instead of $f(3)$.

hints: Putting in $x = 3$ brings in $f(-2)$. Which input brings $f(3)$ back?
Use the two inputs $x = 3$ and $x = -2$, since $1 - 3 = -2$ and $1 - (-2) = 3$. That gives two linear equations in the two unknown values.
You get $f(3) + 3f(-2) = 9$ and $f(-2) - 2f(3) = 4$. Substitute $f(-2) = 4 + 2f(3)$ into the first equation.

solutions.reliable: With $x = 3$: $f(3) + 3f(-2) = 9$. With $x = -2$: $f(-2) - 2f(3) = 4$, so $f(-2) = 4 + 2f(3)$. Substituting, $f(3) + 12 + 6f(3) = 9$, so $7f(3) = -3$ and $f(3) = -\tfrac37$. Check: $f(-2) = 4 - \tfrac67 = \tfrac{22}{7}$, and $-\tfrac37 + 3\cdot\tfrac{22}{7} = \tfrac{63}{7} = 9$. Such an $f$ exists, because for each pair $x, 1 - x$ the system has determinant $1 - x(1 - x) = x^2 - x + 1 > 0$. Transferable idea: when a functional equation links $x$ to $g(x)$ and $g$ undoes itself, substitute both $x$ and $g(x)$ and solve the linear system.
